title: Why Is an Outlet Not Working if the Breaker Did Not Trip?

seo.title: Why Is an Outlet Not Working if the Breaker Did Not Trip?
seo.meta_description: A dead outlet with a normal-looking breaker may be controlled by a wall switch, upstream ground-fault protection, a loose connection, or an internal receptacle fault.
seo.search_intent: Identify why is an outlet not working if the breaker did not trip, use observable clues to choose the first checks, and know when to stop or get professional help.

excerpt: A dead outlet with a normal-looking breaker may be controlled by a wall switch, upstream ground-fault protection, a loose connection, or an internal receptacle fault. Start with external checks and do not remove the cover.
content_html:
A dead outlet with a normal-looking breaker may be controlled by a wall switch, upstream ground-fault protection, a loose connection, or an internal receptacle fault. Start with external checks and do not remove the cover.

Test another device and nearby wall switches

Confirm that the lamp or charger works in another outlet. Some receptacles are controlled by a wall switch, especially in bedrooms and living areas.

Look for a GFCI that may protect it from another location

In North American installations, an outlet may be protected by a ground-fault circuit interrupter (GFCI) located in a bathroom, kitchen, garage, or outside. If it has tripped, address moisture and reset it once using the normal procedure.

Reset a suspect breaker fully off and then on

Some breakers rest in a middle position that is hard to see. If you know the circuit and there is no heat, odor, or visible damage, perform one full reset; if it trips again, do not keep resetting it.

A persistently dead outlet can hide a wiring fault

If switches, GFCI protection, and the breaker are normal but the receptacle stays dead, stop using it and call an electrician. Do not remove the cover or tighten energized connections, especially if other outlets on the circuit are also affected.
